name: XDKNet 3.0.1.2
body:
XDKNet 3.0.1.2 brings invite sign-up onto your own server and fixes Seerr's
webhook setup. Update the server plugin to 3.0.1.2 along with the app.

## Invites without a public Wizarr

- Invite links can now open a sign-up page on your Jellyfin server, at
  /XDKNet/Join/<code>. XDKNet signs the person up through Wizarr behind the
  scenes, so Wizarr can stay on your local network. It is off until you turn
  it on: under Wizarr in the plugin settings, set where invite links open to
  "This server". It needs the Public Server URL to be set.
- The page is locked down: it only works while links point to this server,
  limits how often anyone can try, refuses wrong codes the same way every
  time, lets a one-time invite make only one account, and never shows
  Wizarr's address. Wizarr's steps before sign-up are kept unless you choose
  to skip them.
- When making an invite you can now give Live TV and downloads as well as
  choosing libraries, and the invite list says what each invite gives.

## Settings and fixes

- The Seerr webhook is set up with your Seerr API key, so it no longer waits
  for a Seerr admin to sign in, and its status says what is wrong in words.
- A Public Server URL copied from the web app's address bar is kept as the
  server's address.
- A web address saved as the Wizarr API key is refused with a clear message,
  and the key fields aren't filled in by password managers.

If your server is behind a reverse proxy or tunnel, add its address under
Dashboard > Networking > Known proxies in Jellyfin. Without it the sign-up
page can't tell visitors apart, so it stays closed and the plugin settings
say why.

TVs on 2.4.10 or later offer this update on their own. On 2.4.9, use
Settings > About > Check for updates. Anything older has to install it once
by hand, from the Android TV APK below.
